title: Data sources
intro: KanjiForge is built on open Japanese-language data. The pack files are self-describing; this catalog is the offline screen data.

sources.name: KANJIDIC2
sources.copyright: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, Monash University
sources.use: Kanji literals, codepoints, radicals, grades, stroke counts, frequency, readings, nanori and English meanings.
sources.modification: Converted to SQLite; omitted selected fields and stripped all qc_type=skip and qc_type=misclass entries.

sources.name: JMdict_e (English only)
sources.copyright: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, Monash University
sources.use: English dictionary entries, forms, senses, glosses and commonness tags.
sources.modification: Converted to SQLite with FTS; English-only fields retained, uncommon entries filtered, commonScore derived.

sources.name: JMnedict
sources.copyright: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, Monash University
sources.use: No JMnedict data is present in the current shipped manifests; it is recorded for the optional names pack.

sources.name: KRADFILE / RADKFILE
sources.copyright: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, Monash University
sources.modification: Derived lookup data; the separate RADKFILE archive is pinned in sources.lock.json.

sources.name: RADKFILE
sources.copyright: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, Monash University
sources.modification: Pinned as a separate upstream input; no standalone output pack is currently shipped.

sources.name: KanjiVG
sources.use: Ordered stroke paths, stroke start points and component trees; also input to similar-kanji generation.
sources.modification: Paths normalized to 109x109 and re-encoded; stored separately from CC BY-SA 4.0 packs.

sources.name: Tatoeba Project
sources.use: Japanese sentences, English links and WWWJDIC sense indices; includes Tanaka Corpus JA-EN examples. The pinned sentences_detailed.csv export supplies authors for each retained Japanese and English sentence ID.
sources.modification: Filtered to length 6-30, at least one English translation and at most five per sense, ranked by readability. The sentences pack stores id/ja_author and en_sentence_id/en_author for every shipped pair.

sources.name: JmdictFurigana alignment data
sources.copyright: Doublevil; derived from JMdict / Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, Monash University
sources.licenseName: CC BY-SA 4.0 (JMdict-derived data; repository code is MIT)
sources.use: JMdict-derived per-character furigana alignments for dictionary forms.
sources.modification: Applied alignments to filtered sentence/dictionary records. The upstream repository's MIT code license does not replace CC BY-SA 4.0 obligations for the alignment data.

sources.name: JLPT Kanji Data (davidluzgouveia)
sources.copyright: davidluzgouveia; derived from Jonathan Waller's JLPT Resources
sources.modification: Resolved against the kanji pack and pinned as an explicitly unofficial community estimate.

sources.name: JLPT Vocabulary (yomitan)
sources.copyright: yomitan contributors; derived from Jonathan Waller's JLPT Resources
sources.modification: Resolved against words-core and pinned as an explicitly unofficial community estimate; unresolved entries are reported in jlpt-coverage.json.

sources.name: Noto Serif JP
sources.use: Pinned generator-only font for deterministic similar-kanji rasterization.
sources.modification: A glyph raster is used by the generator; the font itself is not part of the similar JSON pack.

packs.details: Kanji reference SQLite; SKIP and misclassification fields are omitted.
Common-tagged JMdict English dictionary in SQLite with FTS and derived commonScore.
Separate chunked stroke paths, start points and component trees. Paths normalized and re-encoded; six Unicode-range chunks are listed in the manifest.

Filtered JA-EN Tatoeba sentences with stored Japanese/English Tatoeba authors and stable IDs; pairs with unavailable upstream author metadata are excluded. Includes JMdict-derived CC BY-SA 4.0 JmdictFurigana alignment data. The upstream repository's MIT code license does not apply MIT-only terms to alignment data.

Generated lookup: component Jaccard 0.35, stroke proximity 0.15, radical identity 0.15 and 64x64 glyph raster Dice 0.35; threshold 0.48, maximum six matches per character. Derived dataset is ours under CC BY-SA 4.0.

CC BY-SA 4.0 derived deck definitions and coverage report; 25 deck JSON files plus jlpt-coverage.json. JLPT descriptions state that levels are unofficial community estimates. Jōyō 1981 uses the reviewed 196-added/5-removed diff; Jōyō 2010 contains 2,136 characters; school grades 7-9 are frequency tiers; kana decks use words-core.
